characters.name: Daredevil
characters.caseNote: Subject is a blind attorney by day and masked vigilante by night. A radioactive accident cost him his sight and sharpened his other senses. Agents are advised that he is not impressed by cover stories.
characters.notes: Primary team Defenders vs Avengers (New Avengers) or none is arguable. Live-action first appearance is the Matt Murdock cameo in No Way Home (2021).

characters.name: Elektra
characters.caseNote: Subject is a Greek-born assassin trained by the Hand. Has died and returned more often than is administratively convenient. Agents should note her relationship with Daredevil is classified as complicated.
characters.notes: Born Again season 3 (Yung) is unreleased; Garner cameo in Deadpool & Wolverine (2024) is the first qualifying title. Alignment antihero vs villain.

characters.name: Bullseye
characters.caseNote: Subject is a psychopathic assassin who rarely misses with any thrown object. Has served on the Thunderbolts and the Dark Avengers. Agents are advised to hide the paper clips.
characters.notes: Curtis Small plays a Bullseye variant in Deadpool & Wolverine (2024), which precedes Wilson Bethel's Born Again (2025). Alignment villain vs antihero during Thunderbolts/Dark Avengers.

characters.name: Punisher
characters.caseNote: Subject is a former Marine who wages a lethal war on crime after his family was killed. Possesses no superhuman powers, only a large inventory. Agents are advised not to ask about the skull.
characters.notes: Thunderbolts and Savage Avengers memberships were brief and left out.

characters.name: Jessica Jones
characters.caseNote: Subject is a private investigator with super strength and limited flight, acquired in a car accident involving radioactive material. Briefly operated as the hero Jewel. Agents are advised not to expect a warm welcome.
characters.notes: Wikipedia credits Alias #1 (2001); a retcon places her unnamed in Amazing Spider-Man #4 (1963-06). Her Born Again appearance is in season 2.

characters.name: Luke Cage
characters.caseNote: Subject gained unbreakable skin and super strength from a prison experiment. Founded Heroes for Hire and later joined the Avengers. Agents are advised that bullets are a poor opening argument.
characters.notes: Mike Colter appears in Born Again only in the season 2 finale. Netflix's Luke Cage does not count.

characters.name: Iron Fist
characters.caseNote: Subject is a billionaire heir who trained in the mystic city of K'un-L'un. Channels chi into a glowing fist. Agents are advised that he has been described as the Living Weapon, not as a team player.
characters.notes: Finn Jones is credited only in Born Again season 3 (March 2027, unreleased), so mcu is false. Origin magic vs cosmic/mutate is arguable.

characters.name: Misty Knight
characters.caseNote: Subject is a former police detective who lost an arm in a bombing. Replaced it with a Stark-built bionic one. Co-leads the Daughters of the Dragon with Colleen Wing.
characters.notes: Origin tech (bionic arm) vs trained is arguable. Her Netflix appearances do not count.

characters.name: Colleen Wing
characters.caseNote: Subject is a samurai-trained martial artist and the daughter of a Japanese swordsmith. Partner of Misty Knight in the Daughters of the Dragon. Agents are advised not to challenge her to a duel.
characters.notes: Netflix appearances do not count; she is only a wished-for character in Born Again.

characters.name: Typhoid Mary
characters.caseNote: Subject has multiple personalities and telekinetic powers. Has worked as assassin for the Kingpin and the Hand. Agents are advised to ask which personality is on duty.
characters.notes: Origin mutant per Wikipedia infobox; her power source has been retconned over time. Debut as Mutant Zero (2007) is later.

characters.name: Purple Man
characters.caseNote: Subject is a spy whose skin turned purple after a chemical accident and who compels obedience. Menaced Daredevil and Jessica Jones. Agents are advised to decline any request politely worded as an order.
characters.notes: Netflix Jessica Jones does not count toward mcu.

characters.name: Cottonmouth
characters.caseNote: Subject is a Harlem crime boss who filed his teeth into points. A longtime enemy of Luke Cage. Agents are advised that the snake theme is sincere.
characters.notes: Netflix Luke Cage does not count.

characters.name: Diamondback (Willis Stryker)
characters.caseNote: Subject is the former friend whose betrayal sent Luke Cage to prison. Has worked with the Maggia and Hydra. Agents are advised that he carries a grudge and a knife.
characters.notes: Netflix Luke Cage's Diamondback does not count.

characters.name: Black Mariah
characters.caseNote: Subject is a heavyset Harlem criminal and taxi driver with a gang of her own. Opposed Luke Cage. Agents are advised that her cab was not available for hire.
characters.notes: Netflix Luke Cage does not count; Alfre Woodard's Civil War role is a different character.

characters.name: Stick
characters.caseNote: Subject is a blind martial arts master who trained Daredevil. Leads the Chaste against the Hand. Agents are advised that his teaching methods are bluntly practical.
characters.notes: Alignment hero vs antihero is arguable. Netflix appearances do not count.

characters.name: Echo
characters.caseNote: Subject is a deaf Native American martial artist who can copy any motion she sees. Raised by the Kingpin, later turned to heroism. Agents are advised not to try to out-mimic her.
characters.notes: First live-action appearance is Hawkeye (2021), before her own series Echo (2024). Alignment was villain early on.

characters.name: White Tiger (Hector Ayala)
characters.caseNote: Subject is a martial artist who gained tiger-like abilities from mystic amulets. A founding member of the Sons of the Tiger. Agents are advised to leave the amulets alone.
characters.notes: Infobox page is a shared article for several White Tigers; Hector Ayala's debut was used. Origin magic (amulets) vs mutate is arguable.

characters.name: Cloak
characters.caseNote: Subject is a teen runaway whose body connects to a dark dimension. Partner of Dagger. Agents are advised that anything he swallows is not recoverable.
characters.notes: Freeform's Cloak & Dagger does not count. Teams left empty; no iconic non-pair team.

characters.name: Dagger
characters.caseNote: Subject is a runaway who produces knives of light that cleanse drugs and violence. Partner of Cloak. Agents are advised her cutlery cannot be confiscated.
characters.notes: Freeform's Cloak & Dagger does not count.

characters.name: Shang-Chi
characters.mcuFirst: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings
characters.caseNote: Subject is a martial arts master and son of Fu Manchu in his original comics. Rejected his father's criminal empire. Agents are advised that he is, in fact, not Bruce Lee.

characters.name: Jigsaw
characters.caseNote: Subject is a mobster whose face was scarred in a fight with the Punisher. Menaces both the Punisher and Spider-Man. Agents are advised he is a good deal more patient than he appears.
characters.notes: Debut is the cameo in Amazing Spider-Man #161; full appearance is #162. Netflix The Punisher does not count.

characters.name: Night Nurse
characters.caseNote: Subject is a trained nurse who treats superheroes and others who cannot visit a hospital. Is not herself superpowered. Agents are advised she keeps no records.
characters.notes: Candidate resolves to Linda Carter; debut as Linda Carter (1961-09) vs as Night Nurse (Night Nurse #1, 1972-11 or Daredevil #58). Christine Palmer in Doctor Strange is a different character.

characters.name: Hellcat
characters.caseNote: Subject began as a teen comic star and later became a costumed adventurer. Has served on the Avengers and the Defenders. Agents are advised she has outlived multiple genres.
characters.notes: Debut is as Patsy Walker (1944); Hellcat debuted in Avengers #144 (1976-02). Origin mutate (infobox) vs tech (Cat costume) is arguable. Primary team Defenders vs Avengers is arguable.

characters.name: Nighthawk (Kyle Richmond)
characters.caseNote: Subject is a wealthy heir who drank an alchemy serum for strength at night. Has served as a villain, as a Defender and as a Thunderbolt. Agents are advised that his loyalties vary by decade.
characters.notes: Origin mutate (serum) vs trained is arguable; alignment villain/antihero/hero. Squadron Supreme counted in otherTeams because the Earth-616 version was a simulacrum.

characters.name: Muse
characters.caseNote: Subject is a serial killer who stages mass killings into street art. His ghost later guided a second Muse. Agents are advised not to critique the work.
characters.notes: Two Muses: first is Inhuman Vincent van Gore (used), second Morgan Whittier is human (debut 2025). Born Again season 1 depicts Bastian Cooper as the Muse killer; Heather Glenn's Muse is season 3.

characters.name: Gladiator (Melvin Potter)
characters.caseNote: Subject is a tailor who builds his own costumes with spinning blades on the hands. Fought Daredevil on several occasions. Agents are advised not to hand him fabric shears.
characters.notes: Origin tech (blades and armor) vs trained is arguable. The Gladiator in Thor: Ragnarok is unrelated.

characters.name: Lady Bullseye
characters.caseNote: Subject is a lawyer turned assassin inspired by Bullseye. Trained in martial arts and a skilled marksman. Agents are advised that her briefcase is not for filing.
characters.notes: Wikipedia gives few affiliations; Hand membership noted as informal.

characters.name: Bushmaster
characters.caseNote: Subject is a Maggia crime figure whose Power Man treatment turned him into living metal. Opposed Luke Cage and Iron Fist. Agents are advised he is not a snake, despite the name.
characters.notes: Two Bushmasters; John McIver (Iron Fist #15) used. Mustafa Shakir's Luke Cage role is Netflix and does not count.

characters.name: The Owl
characters.caseNote: Subject is a former financier who used a serum to gain strength and glide on air currents. Bald and fond of owl-themed capes. Agents are advised he did not pay his taxes.
characters.notes: Bob Gunton's Daredevil role is Netflix and does not count.

characters.name: Paladin
characters.caseNote: Subject is a mercenary who sells his services to whomever pays. Has worked with Heroes for Hire and the Thunderbolts. Agents are advised to check the invoice.
characters.notes: Todd Stashwick appears as Paladin in VisionQuest (2026-10-13). Alignment antihero vs hero is arguable.

dropped.name: Madame Gao
dropped.reason: Not a Marvel Comics (Earth-616) character and has no Wikipedia article; she debuted in Netflix's Daredevil (2015), which does not count for the MCU, and the infobox resolved to Stick.
